items.key_claim: AWS 和 Azure 的高价主要来自按需定价，而 neocloud 主要是合约定价，两者不能简单解读为 neocloud 在“低价抢单”。

items.summary: 对 neocloud 与传统云的价格比较提出修正：AWS、Azure 的 GPU 价格更像按需服务定价，本来就应更贵；而 Nebius、CoreWeave 这类 neocloud 更多是合约式定价。结论是相关行业数据不能直接得出 neocloud 在全面“压价抢市场”，更准确的理解是商业模式和计费结构不同。

summary_i18n.en: This pushes back on direct price comparisons between neoclouds and hyperscalers: GPU pricing at AWS and Azure reflects on-demand service pricing and should naturally be higher, while neoclouds like Nebius and CoreWeave rely more on contract-based pricing. The takeaway is that the data should not be read as simple across-the-board price undercutting by neoclouds; the more accurate interpretation is that the business models and billing structures are different.

summary_i18n.en: CRDO reports FY27 Q1 after the close on Sept. 1. In the prior quarter, FY26 Q4 revenue was $437M, up 157% YoY, with 68.3% non-GAAP gross margin and $177.5M of free cash flow; full-year revenue reached $1.335B, up 206%, helping drive roughly a 21% stock gain in the first week of August and pushing price targets up to a Street-high $350. For this quarter, management guided to $465-475M revenue, about 111% YoY growth, with 67-69% non-GAAP gross margin, while reaffirming over 80% FY27 revenue growth and optics revenue above $600M. The trade focus is whether margins hold, whether expansion to a fifth hyperscaler reduces the current top-three customer concentration of 34%/27%/16%, and whether the H2 FY27 optical inflection remains on track after the DustPhotonics integration. items.summary: CPO scale-out交换机预计从2025年的5000台增至2030年的20万台，144%CAGR，且2027-2028年需求几乎集中在100T和200T这类最高密度、最高光学含量的交换机。每台都需要高功率激光器，因此产业链受益重点落在上游激光器环节：$COHR 与 $LITE 已是CPO激光器已知主力供应商，并获得 $NVDA 约40亿美元合计投资以锁定产能；$AAOI 当前规模较小，但正建设自有激光器制造能力，已出货400mW/25dBm产品，贴合CPO需求。核心判断是高功率激光器供给稀缺，谁能真正扩出产能，谁就能抓住这轮CPO放量曲线。

summary_i18n.en: Scale-out CPO switch units are projected to rise from 5,000 in 2025 to 200,000 by 2030, a 144% CAGR, with demand through 2027-2028 concentrated in 100T and 200T switches that carry the highest density and optical content. Each switch requires high-power lasers, so the main beneficiaries are upstream laser suppliers: $COHR and $LITE are already recognized leaders in CPO laser sourcing and have roughly $4 billion of combined investment from $NVDA to lock in capacity; $AAOI is smaller today but is building in-house laser manufacturing and has already shipped 400mW/25dBm lasers that fit CPO requirements. The core view is that high-power laser supply is scarce, and the companies that can actually scale production will capture this CPO demand curve.
